name: Uthai
overview: Uthai was a male descendant of Bigvai who participated in the return to Jerusalem with Ezra, as recorded in Ezra 8:14. Although his tribal affiliation and additional details are not specified, his inclusion in the list of returnees highlights his role in the restoration of the Jewish community after the exile. The biblical record provides limited information beyond his ancestry and participation in this significant event.
namesAndTitles: The name Uthai likely means either 'superiority of YHWH' or '[my] restoration,' reflecting themes of divine supremacy and renewal. This proper name, as given in Ezra 8:14, carries spiritual significance consistent with the context of the return from exile and God's faithfulness in restoration.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Uthai was a descendant of Bigvai, establishing a clear genealogical connection. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Uthai's significance lies in his role among those who returned to Jerusalem under Ezra's leadership, demonstrating faithfulness to God's call to rebuild the community and worship rightly. His lineage from Bigvai connects him to a family involved in this pivotal moment of restoration. Through his participation, Uthai exemplifies the obedience and hope that characterized the post-exilic return and renewal of Israel.
